properties.title: Ben Uri Gallery
properties.description: Ben Uri holds Europe’s only collection dedicated to Jewish, refugee and immigrant artists, comprising around 880 works by approximately 380 artists from 45 countries of birth. The collection includes artists whose lives were shaped by racial, political and artistic persecution under Nazi rule, including Kindertransportees. Its paintings, drawings, prints and sculpture, alongside biographical and reference material, provide insight into experiences of persecution and migration, as well as the contribution of refugee and immigrant artists to British visual culture.

properties.title: Bodleian Library
properties.description: The Bodleian Libraries are one of the world's leading research libraries, with internationally significant archival and special collections. Their Their Finest Hour archive is one of the UK's largest digital collections of Second World War stories, comprising approximately 2,000 stories and more than 25,000 digitised items. These include photographs, correspondence, diaries, memoirs and oral testimony from Jewish refugees, Kindertransport survivors, civilian internees and British servicemen involved in the liberation of concentration camps.

properties.title: Bristol Archives
properties.description: Bristol Archives holds extensive public and private archival collections spanning local, national and international history. Its Holocaust-related collections include records of refugee support in Bristol, personal papers relating to British military service and prisoner of war experiences, correspondence between British civilians and German prisoners of war, and oral histories of Jewish migration to Mandate Palestine and the humanitarian consequences of Nazi persecution.

properties.title: Brunel, University of London
properties.description: Brunel University London holds the archive of Heinz Wolff, who served as Professor of Bioengineering there. The collection traces his life from his escape from Nazi Germany with his father to his career in Britain. Personal papers, correspondence, photographs and professional records document his experiences as a Jewish refugee alongside his contributions to bioengineering and science communication.

properties.title: Cambridge University Library
properties.description: The Department of Archives and Modern Manuscripts at Cambridge University Library holds two complementary collections documenting assistance to refugees escaping Nazi persecution from the late 1930s onwards. The first comprises the records of the Cambridge Refugee Committee, preserving committee minutes, correspondence, refugee registers and administrative papers relating primarily to Jewish refugees from Germany, Austria and Czechoslovakia. The second documents Margareta Burkill's work with German and Austrian refugee children through memoirs, correspondence and case notes tracing their wartime accommodation and post-war resettlement.

properties.title: Churchill Archives Centre
properties.description: The Churchill Archives Centre preserves the personal papers of many of the twentieth century's leading politicians, diplomats, lawyers, humanitarian workers and military figures, including Sir Winston Churchill. Its Holocaust-related holdings are distributed across numerous collections and include correspondence, government papers, case histories, photographs and personal archives documenting British responses to Nazi persecution, the liberation of concentration camps, refugee relief and resettlement, the Nuremberg Trials, and the development of international criminal law.

properties.title: Durham University
properties.description: Durham University Library's Archives and Special Collections houses internationally significant manuscript and archival collections spanning more than a millennium of history. Its Holocaust-related holdings include the papers of the German-Jewish historian Wilhelm Levison documenting academic exile, Nazi persecution, emigration, post-war restitution, and the experiences of German-Jewish refugees through correspondence, personal papers, official documents and photographs. There is also material relating to the Backhaus family and Nazi indoctrination.

properties.title: Gathering The Voices
properties.description: Gathering the Voices preserves firsthand oral testimonies from people who experienced the Holocaust and subsequently found sanctuary in Scotland. The collection follows the experiences of those who fled Nazi persecution, including Kindertransportees and adult refugees, as well as Holocaust survivors, from their experiences of persecution and displacement through to rebuilding their lives. The testimonies also explore the ways in which refugees established careers, families and communities in Scotland while reflecting on the experiences and losses that shaped their lives.

properties.title: Gloucestershire County Council (Gloucestershire Heritage Hub)
properties.description: Gloucestershire Heritage Hub preserves the archival heritage of Gloucestershire through collections documenting the county's communities, organisations and local history. Its Holocaust-related holdings centre on Gloucestershire's response to refugees fleeing Nazi persecution, particularly through the work of the Gloucester Association for Aiding Refugees. They also document the experiences of Kindertransport survivors, refugee resettlement in the county, and the continuing commemoration of the Holocaust through organisational records, personal papers, oral histories and commemorative material.

properties.title: Historic Environment Scotland
properties.description: Historic Environment Scotland manages the National Collection of Aerial Photography (NCAP), a digital archive of more than 30 million aerial photographs accessible through an interactive map interface. Through collections such as the Allied Central Interpretation Unit (ACIU) and German Air Force (GX) archives, NCAP provides access to millions of Second World War aerial reconnaissance images documenting occupied Europe and sites associated with the Holocaust.

properties.title: Holocaust Centre North
properties.description: Holocaust Centre North is an archive, exhibition and learning centre that preserves the records of the Holocaust Survivors' Friendship Association (HSFA). Its collections include the organisational records of HSFA alongside more than 150 personal archives of Holocaust survivors, their descendants and associates connected to the north of England, documenting experiences of persecution, survival, displacement, resettlement and Holocaust remembrance.

properties.title: Imperial War Museum London
properties.description: The Imperial War Museum holds one of the United Kingdom's largest collections relating to the Holocaust within its wider holdings on twentieth-century conflict. Holocaust-related material is preserved across every major collecting department, including personal and oral testimonies, official records, military documentation, photographs, film, artworks, objects and library collections. Together, these holdings document Nazi persecution, refugee experiences, concentration camps, liberation, the Nuremberg Trials and Holocaust remembrance.

properties.title: Jersey Heritage
properties.description: Jersey Heritage's archival, museum and library collections include significant holdings relating to Jersey's history as one of the only parts of the British Isles to experience Nazi occupation during the Second World War. Its holdings include archival records, oral histories, publications, photographs and exhibition material relating to the deportation of Jersey's Jewish inhabitants, Jewish refugee experiences, acts of rescue, and Holocaust commemoration.

properties.title: King's College, Taunton
properties.description: King's College Taunton preserves the historical records of the school, including administrative records, photographs and material relating to former pupils and school life. The archive includes material relating to fifteen German-Jewish pupils who were offered assisted places at the school from 1936, documenting the admission and education of refugee children fleeing Nazi persecution.

properties.title: Lake District Holocaust Project
properties.description: The Lake District Holocaust Project has developed an extensive archive documenting the arrival of the 300 child Holocaust survivors brought to Calgarth Estate, Windermere, in 1945. Through survivor testimonies, photographs, correspondence, personal artefacts, archival records and archaeological material, the collections document both the experiences of the children as they rebuilt their lives in Britain and the community that welcomed them. Together, these records preserve the interconnected histories and legacy of the Windermere Children and the local community.

properties.title: Library of the Society of Friends
properties.description: The Library of the Society of Friends preserves the archives of Quakers in Britain, spanning the Society's activities nationwide, alongside extensive library and manuscript collections documenting their humanitarian activity. The collections include records on refugee relief, support for people fleeing Nazi persecution, Kindertransport, and relief work during and after the Second World War.

properties.title: Liverpool Record Office
properties.description: Liverpool Record Office preserves extensive archival collections relating to Liverpool's Jewish community, including the records of organisations established to support refugees fleeing Nazi persecution. Alongside personal papers, correspondence and commemorative material, the collections document Jewish refugee relief, support for the Kindertransport, Holocaust survivors, liberation, remembrance, and the post-war experiences of refugees in Merseyside.

properties.title: London College of Communications (University Archives and Special Collections Centre)
properties.description: The University Archives and Special Collections Centre at London College of Communication preserves internationally significant collections relating to photography, graphic design, film and visual culture. Among its holdings is the Stanley Kubrick Archive, which preserves screenplay drafts, historical visual research, production material, and an extensive research library of books and memoirs assembled for the unmade film Aryan Papers, documenting Kubrick's research into the Holocaust and the persecution of Polish Jews under Nazi occupation.

properties.title: Manx National Heritage
properties.description: Manx National Heritage preserves the archives, library and museum collections of the Isle of Man, including extensive holdings relating to the Second World War civilian internment camps established by the British government on the island. The collections comprise official records, personal papers, correspondence, memoirs, photographs, ephemera, camp newspapers and museum objects documenting the internment of refugees fleeing Nazi persecution who were subsequently classified as 'enemy aliens', some of whom were Jewish, alongside the wider history of civilian internment.

properties.title: Museum of Liverpool
properties.description: The Museum of Liverpool preserves material culture, archives and community collections documenting the history of Liverpool and its people. The collections document the experiences and remembrance of Merseyside's Holocaust survivor and refugee communities through personal testimony, commemorative publications, textiles and community artworks. They also include material relating to Project Triangle, a cultural exchange programme exploring the Holocaust, the persecution of LGBTQ+ people under Nazism, and the continuing impact of these histories on discussions of homophobia and hate crime.

properties.title: Parkes Special Collections, University of Southampton
properties.description: The Parkes Collections at the University of Southampton comprise one of the world's foremost archival and library resources for the study of Jewish and non-Jewish relations. Established by the Reverend Dr James Parkes, the collections include his papers on antisemitism alongside the records of Anglo-Jewish organisations, refugee and relief bodies, Jewish communal institutions and individuals. Holocaust-related material includes correspondence, organisational records and personal papers documenting antisemitism, responses to Nazism, refugee rescue and resettlement, and the experiences of Holocaust survivors and their descendants.

properties.title: Public Records Office Northern Ireland
properties.description: The Public Record Office of Northern Ireland (PRONI) preserves the documentary heritage of Northern Ireland through government, private and community archives. Its Holocaust-related holdings document Northern Ireland's role in supporting Jewish refugees during the Holocaust through official records, immigration documentation, correspondence and administrative papers relating to refugee migration, sponsorship, government decision-making and refugee assistance.

properties.title: Queen's University Belfast Special Collections
properties.description: Queen's University Belfast Special Collections & Archives preserves extensive collections documenting Jewish life and identity in Northern Ireland. The collections comprise the archives of individuals, families and Jewish communal organisations, including multilingual correspondence, personal papers and institutional records documenting refugee movements, Jewish relief efforts, religious life and Northern Ireland's connections to the wider history of the Holocaust.

properties.title: Royal College of Physicians Archive
properties.description: The Royal College of Physicians Archive preserves the institutional records of the College alongside the personal and professional papers of leading physicians and medical organisations. Its Holocaust-related holdings focus on the investigation of Nazi medical experimentation, preserving committee records, correspondence and reports relating to post-war British efforts to investigate Nazi medical war crimes.

properties.title: Scottish Jewish Archives Centre
properties.description: The Scottish Jewish Archives Centre preserves records relating to the history and experiences of Jewish communities in Scotland. Its Holocaust-related collections are extensive and document the experience of Jewish refugees who arrived during the 1930s and 1940s, including Kindertransportees and those who came on domestic service visas, as well as those interned as ‘enemy aliens’ and concentration camp survivors. Personal and family papers, photographs, identity documents, correspondence, refugee hostel records and oral testimonies provide material on persecution, flight and internment, as well as the experiences of refugees rebuilding their lives and communities in Scotland.

properties.title: Senate House Library
properties.description: Senate House Library preserves extensive archival, manuscript and special collections supporting research across the humanities and social sciences. The collections include the papers of German-speaking Jewish refugees, exile organisations and refugee scholars, including correspondence, personal papers and organisational records documenting displacement, exile, forced migration and the intellectual and cultural lives of those who fled Nazi persecution.

properties.title: Soldiers of Oxfordshire Museum
properties.description: The Soldiers of Oxfordshire Museum preserves archives, photographs, objects and personal papers documenting the military history of Oxfordshire regiments and the people who served in them. The collections include material relating to the liberation of Nazi concentration camps, the experiences of Holocaust survivors encountered by British soldiers, and the personal relationships that developed between liberators and survivors in the aftermath of the Second World War.

properties.title: St Helens Archive Service
properties.description: St Helens Archive Service preserves a personal collection relating to the liberation of Bergen-Belsen concentration camp, comprising letters and photographs created during the service of James Cotton of St Helens with the 11th Light Field Ambulance in 1945. The collection documents the clearance of the camp and its immediate aftermath through the perspective of a British serviceman.

properties.title: Suffolk Archives
properties.description: Suffolk Archives preserves collections documenting the experiences of Jewish refugees who sought refuge in Suffolk before and during the Second World War. Through memoirs, personal papers, photographs and community history material, the collections document refugee life at Palace House Stables in Newmarket, the Kindertransport, the internment of 'enemy aliens', and wider wartime experiences through military service records, prisoner-of-war material and personal papers.

properties.title: Tate Galleries
properties.description: The Tate Archive preserves the papers of artists, curators, critics and gallery staff documenting the history of British art. The collections include artists' papers, correspondence, exhibition files and institutional records relating to Jewish refugee artists, Holocaust memorialisation, antisemitism, and the representation of the Holocaust in modern and contemporary art.

properties.title: Templeman Library, University of Kent
properties.description: Templeman Library Special Collections & Archives preserves nationally significant collections relating to British political and social history. Holocaust-related holdings include the work of cartoonist Carl Giles within the British Cartoon Archive, documenting representations of Nazism, the Second World War and the Holocaust in British political and social cartoons. The collections also include the UK Philanthropy Archive, which holds the papers of Kindertransport refugee Dame Stephanie Shirley, documenting her life, philanthropy and refugee experience.

properties.title: The Box, Plymouth
properties.description: The Box holds collections documenting the arrival and support of Jewish refugees in Plymouth during the Second World War and the history of the city's Jewish community. Holdings include the records of the Society of Friends Refugee Committee, including refugee case files, correspondence and printed material, together with the archives of Plymouth Hebrew Congregation, the Jacob Nathan Congregational School and the Hebrew Board of Guardians.

properties.title: The British Library
properties.description: The British Library holds a major collection of Holocaust survivor oral histories within its Sound Archive. The collection comprises 289 life story interviews and over 1,000 hours of recordings documenting pre-war Jewish life, Nazi persecution, ghettos, concentration camps, resistance, Kindertransport, liberation and post-war resettlement. Fully digitised and accessible through British Library Sounds, the recordings are searchable by theme and provide worldwide access to first-hand survivor testimony.

properties.title: The British Psychoanalytical Society Archive
properties.description: The British Psychoanalytical Society Archive holds collections documenting the displacement and resettlement of psychoanalysts following Nazi persecution, together with the development of psychoanalytic responses to the experiences of war and displacement. The collections comprise organisational records, correspondence, personal and professional papers relating to refugee assistance, the emigration of psychoanalysts from continental Europe, and psychoanalytic work with children affected by evacuation, separation and the Second World War.

properties.title: The Glasgow School of Art
properties.description: The Glasgow School of Art Archives and Collections holds collections documenting the experiences and artistic legacies of Jewish refugees who settled in Britain after fleeing Nazi persecution. Through institutional records, correspondence, artists' papers, architectural archives and artworks, the collections trace the education, careers and creative contributions of refugee artists, architects and students, including Josef Herman and Isi Metzstein.

properties.title: The Keep, University of Sussex
properties.description: The Keep holds significant collections documenting the experiences of Jewish refugees from Germany and Austria alongside collections relating to resistance against Nazi occupation in France. Through personal papers, correspondence, family archives, memoirs, artwork and oral testimonies, the collections document persecution, forced migration, internment, resistance, exile and post-war remembrance.

properties.title: The London Archives
properties.description: The London Archives holds the archives of major Jewish communal organisations in London, documenting support for Jewish refugees before, during and after the Holocaust. The collections comprise organisational records, personal papers, synagogue archives, school records and welfare organisation records, tracing refugee assistance, resettlement, Jewish communal life and the responses of London's Jewish community to Nazi persecution in continental Europe.

properties.title: The National Archives
properties.description: The National Archives holds government records documenting Britain's diplomatic, military and administrative responses to Nazi persecution and the Holocaust. The collections comprise Foreign Office, Home Office, War Office and Cabinet Office records, together with captured German records, tracing refugee policy, internment, the liberation of concentration camps, and Allied occupation and war crimes investigations.

properties.title: The Salvation Army
properties.description: The Salvation Army International Heritage Centre holds collections documenting the organisation's humanitarian responses to the Second World War and its aftermath. The collections comprise organisational records, correspondence, reports, photographs and personal papers relating to wartime relief, displaced populations, post-war reconstruction and international welfare work in response to Nazi persecution and its aftermath.

properties.title: The Warburg Institute
properties.description: The Warburg Institute Archive documents the relocation of the Warburg Institute from Hamburg to London in 1933 following the Nazi rise to power and the forced exile of German-Jewish scholars. Its institutional records, personal papers and photographic collections support research into the displacement of Jewish academics, the preservation of Jewish cultural heritage, and the visual and intellectual traditions threatened under Nazism through extensive photographic documentation of Jewish ritual, synagogues, cemeteries, ghettos and material culture.

properties.title: The Wiener Holocaust Library
properties.description: The Wiener Holocaust Library is one of the world's foremost archives on the Holocaust, the Nazi era and related themes. Its collection of more than one million items includes published and unpublished works, personal papers, organisational archives, photographs, eyewitness testimonies, press cuttings and ephemera documenting Jewish life before the Holocaust, Nazi persecution, refugee experiences, the Holocaust and its aftermath.

properties.title: Topolski Studio
properties.description: The Topolski Studio preserves the archive of the Polish-Jewish artist Feliks Topolski, who served as an official war artist for the Polish government-in-exile and later the British government during the Second World War. Holocaust-related holdings include original drawings produced at Papenberg and Bergen-Belsen concentration camps within a week of their liberation in 1945, together with drawings from the Nuremberg Trials.

properties.title: Tower Hamlets Local History Library and Archives
properties.description: Tower Hamlets Local History Library and Archives preserves archival collections relating to the history of the London Borough of Tower Hamlets and its communities. Holocaust-related holdings include the Levi family papers relating to Hilda Levi, who escaped Nazi Germany as a child, and her father, Dr Friedrich Hermann Levi, who was murdered during the Holocaust, documenting the persecution and separation of a German-Jewish family.

properties.title: UCL Special Collections
properties.description: UCL Special Collections preserves nationally significant archives, manuscripts and printed collections spanning Jewish studies, politics, literature and science. The Institute of Jewish Affairs Archive documents Nazi Germany, the persecution of European Jews and the Eichmann Trial through publications, reports and press material. Further material includes papers of the German-Jewish Altmann family, documenting their flight from Nazi Germany, and records of the Jewish Refugees Aid Society Committee relating to refugee assistance in Britain.

properties.title: University of East Anglia
properties.description: The University of East Anglia's Archives and Special Collections preserves literary, personal, political and design archives. Its collections include the Patricia Crampton Archive, comprising correspondence relating to Patricia Crampton's work as a document translator at the Nuremberg War Crimes Trials, and the Pritchard Papers, documenting the work of entrepreneur Jack Pritchard, including his assistance to refugees fleeing fascism and his connections with émigré architects and designers who escaped Nazi Germany.

properties.title: University of Hull
properties.description: The Hull History Centre, a partnership between the University of Hull and Hull City Council, preserves nationally significant political and campaigning archives alongside personal papers. Material documenting British responses to fascism, anti-Semitism, refugees and post-war relief is held within the records of Liberty (formerly the National Council for Civil Liberties) and the International Voluntary Service. The personal papers of refugee cartoonist Victor Weisz ('Vicky') provide an individual perspective on exile, alongside records relating to refugees and political detainees in Nazi-occupied Czechoslovakia.

properties.title: University of Lancaster
properties.description: Lancaster University Library's Special Collections & Archives preserves collections relating to regional, literary, political and musical history. Among its holdings is the Hans Ferdinand Redlich Collection, comprising the personal papers, music library and annotated scores of Austrian-Jewish musicologist, conductor and composer Hans Ferdinand Redlich, who fled Nazi persecution following the Anschluss and rebuilt his academic and musical career in Britain. The collections also include material relating to Quaker humanitarian relief and refugee assistance during and after the Second World War.

properties.title: University of Leicester
properties.description: The University of Leicester's Archives and Special Collections preserves archival collections relating to the history of the university and the East Midlands’ wider cultural and social history. Holocaust-related holdings include the East Midlands Oral History Archive, documenting the liberation of Bergen-Belsen and Holocaust remembrance through oral history interviews, and the papers of Helga-Maria and Irene Bejach, which detail the experiences of two German-Jewish sisters who arrived in Britain on the Kindertransport in 1939.

properties.title: University of Nottingham
properties.description: The University of Nottingham's Manuscripts and Special Collections preserve over 800 archive and manuscript collections spanning political, literary and cultural history. The collections include the papers of Austrian-Jewish refugee families Albert and Christl Tugendhat and Bernhard Steinitz, alongside Nazi-era German schoolbooks and records relating to the British Military Government in post-war Berlin, documenting Jewish exile, Nazi ideology and the aftermath of the Second World War.

properties.title: Wilhelmina Barns-Graham Trust
properties.description: The Wilhelmina Barns-Graham Trust preserves the personal and artistic archive of the artist Wilhelmina Barns-Graham. Holocaust-related holdings include correspondence, photographs, drawings and personal papers relating to her friendship with Robert Wagner, a German-Jewish refugee who fled Nazi Germany for the United States in 1938 before returning to Europe as a soldier in the US Army. The collection also documents the fate of Wagner's family during the Holocaust, including the murder of his mother and sister, and his own death following the D-Day landings.
